text: - Board members, please take your seats.

Good evening and welcome to the public hearing on the superintendent's proposed school boundary adjustments. On behalf of the entire school board, I would like to thank you for sharing your comments with us. This hearing is being broadcast on channel 99 and live streamed on YouTube and on our website at www.fcps.edu/livestream.

At the January 8th, 2026 regular meeting, Dr. Reed presented her boundary adjustment recommendations on Saturday January 10th and January 10th or 13th 2026 the board heard the school board heard comments on on the proposal at a public hearing and this public hearing is another opportunity for those comments as well at this time I call on Dr. Reed for a statement.

Thank you madam chair this evening just want to thank our community for coming out to comment We've heard a lot of feedback over the last 18 months, and while I think Scenario 4 was the last formal scenario that we took back to the community very recently in November and December, and after hearing feedback from the community about Scenario 4, we made further adjustments and those were reflected in what I presented as an amended recommendation at our last board hearing on boundaries and at this point we've made no further

adjustments to the to that amended recommendation and we do look forward to hearing comments this evening and really appreciate the breadth and depth of community engagement in a really complex process so we also recognize that this particular round is not perfect and we can't let perfection get in the way of of progress we know that as we have further cycles of review and further iterations the boundaries I think will become refined and continue to be improved over time so we look forward to engaging in that process with some

spots for January of 2027 which is in the document linked on the website and others where we will be able to prep for the next five-year cycle and we look forward to ample time to be really ready for the next five years so thank you madam chair thank you dr reed we have 32 pre-registered and walk-in speakers who will address the board at this public hearing speakers are allotted two minutes and we ask that you stay within your time limit the timer will start when you begin to speak and the timer will sound after two minutes please ensure that your remarks are limited to the proposed school boundary adjustments and that your remarks adhere to the school board's expectation for community participation

including in those expectations are that only one person is allowed at the podium when speaking. Neither adults nor children may accompany a speaker to the podium. Copies of all expectations are available at the back of the auditorium. To assist with the flow of tonight's hearing, please ensure that you are following along with the speaker list and please be ready to go as soon as your name is called. If you have a hard copy of your testimony, please give it to the clerk. If you are virtual, please turn on your camera when you are the next in line to speak so that you just have to unmute when you are called to speak.

If you have electronic copies of your testimony and would like to share it with the board, please email it to communityparticipation@fcps.edu. When your name is called, the clerk will read your name three times before moving on to the next individual on the list. You may find copies of the speaking order at the back of the room or on board docs. We ask for grace and patience from the audience members and we also ask you to to hold applause so that we keep the hearing flowing to ensure that all speakers are heard in a timely manner.

School board members may be taking small breaks, but are able to access the hearing throughout the building and will be listening to all speakers. Madam Clerk, please call our first speaker. - Ashley Vandebunte.

I'm a Cardinal Forest parent. I want to thank Dr. Reed and the school board for pausing the proposed boundary adjustment for Cardinal Forest Elementary School. This late change in Scenario 4, introduced at a time when Cardinal Forest is without a brought-up school board representative, would have increased the school's capacity from 102 percent to 108 percent an outcome that somehow went unnoticed this runs counter to the stated goals of the review which includes balancing available capacity to make the best use of our school facilities the scenario placed a disproportionate capacity burden on one elementary school no other school in the west springfield pyramid or even in the surrounding area has experienced an increase in capacity under this area the adjustment neglected to consider cardinal

forests is comprised of nearly 2 400 townhomes condominiums and other more affordable housing options compared to the areas and other areas in the pyramid whose boundaries and capacity levels remain largely the same this placed additional strain on a community that already faces greater resource constraints and may have less time or flexibility to attend these meetings and advocate for their school while educators families and students are doing their best to handle the already over capacity school increasing the capacity to 108 would harm student well-being through increased stress and anxiety from crowded spaces and potentially more behavioral challenges academically it would mean larger class sizes with less individualized instruction

resource strains and an increased strain on teachers making retention recruitment harder overcrowding negatively impacts student outcomes the last proposal asked cardinal forest to absorb nearly all that burden for the entire west springfield pyramid in order to preserve preferred pyramid boundaries for others easing and balancing overcrowding must be a top priority for the board as it directly impacts the quality of education a student receives and a concentrated effort should be made by the board to avoid overburdening one school. Thank you. I appreciate Dr. Lee and the school board for listening and pausing this change. I urge you to fully consider these factors during the next year's review and to commit to not pushing Cardinal Forrest for their over capacity. Thank
you again. Megan Neforas. First of the board, my name is Megan Neforas. I've been a CPS employee for 16 years, but I speak to you today as a parent from Cardinal Forrest Elementary.

The recent proposal to increase our capacity from 102 percent to 108 percent failed to consider the unique needs of our diverse and transient community i'm asking for that to not happen again currently cardinal forest is already bursting at the seams my fourth grader and his entire grade level are currently in modulars and special classes are pushed into trailers some of the classrooms already have 30 students my sixth grader is an advanced math class with 33 students had three students not been identified to complete algebra one delivered through admitum there would would be 36 students in that room for a teacher to support. In the modular units, teachers

share that students lose approximately 10 minutes of instruction just to use the bathroom. In the cafeteria, the overcrowding is so severe that children feel forced to choose between finishing what could be one of their only meals of the day or having recess, as they are often standing in line right up until the end of lunch. For a Title I adjacent community, asking a child to choose between nutrition and play is a logistical failure and a social injustice. The county's strategic plan includes a vision to increase academic rigor but you cannot have rigor without relationships and support. Cardinal Forest is the only elementary school in the West Springfield pyramid with five specialized special education programs including

the only preschool autism program. Close to 20 percent of our students are multilingual learners, 24 percent receive special education services, and 12 percent are military connected. Our diverse learners require individual attention and quality relationships with teachers that simply will vanish when they are overwhelmed by sheer numbers and limited space when you crowd classrooms behavior conflicts rise mental health needs escalate and the quality of instruction fails we will lose our best educators to exhaustion and our students will lose the joy and foundation of their education i'm asking the board to work with us to create a transparent plan that actually

reduces the existing strain on our building for our mighty Redbird Madeline Grenier good evening members of the school board my name is Maddie Greiner I'm the Belvedere Elementary PTA president and the parent of four Belvedere students first I want to thank you for postponing the proposed

boundary changes affecting Belvedere as originally presented those changes would have made Belvedere a triple split feeder sending students to three different middle schools and three different high schools we appreciate the board's will willingness to listen to families and educators and to hit pause on an issue with significant community impact at the same time postponing the decision doesn't eliminate its effects it simply moves them forward families and staff are still love trying to understand what a future split feeder plan could mean for our school community at Belvedere relationships matter students succeed because teachers know them families are connected and the community is stable but a split feeder model disrupts that it separates peers

that grew up together complicates the transition to middle school and creates uncertainty for families. It also places additional burdens on educators who must coordinate across a school pyramid to maintain continuity, consistency, and positive transitions in and for the curriculum. As you continue this work, we respectfully ask for meaningful opportunities to engage early and meaningfully before decisions are effectively final. We want to understand the goals, review the data, and share what we see every day, how these changes affect students socially and emotionally, how they affect staffing and school climate, and how they affect families ability to plan for their children's education beyond

elementary school we're not here to dismiss the challenges FCPS is working to address we understand capacity and equity matter we simply ask that any future changes involving the Belvedere community be developed with transparent communication clear timelines and genuine partnership so families and educators aren't left reacting at the last minute thank you for your time and for continuing to consider the impact on Belvedere students staff and family

about our son our schools in our neighborhood and respectfully ask the board not to change Belvedere Glasgow justice school pyramid for our neighborhood as a family we deep that deeply values diversity one of the primary reasons we chose to invest in Barker of Woods is the school pyramid which we are assigned to not only excels academically as an IB and AAP center, but it's also widely recognized for its diversity, inclusion, and equity.

Our son is 11 years old and part of the last cohort whose early education was profoundly disrupted by COVID. Belvedere Elementary became his second home, a place of stability with administrators and staff who worked hardlessly to help students catch up. Dr. Reed, you met our son last year when you visited the school.

He was the fifth grade ambassador during your visit an impactful experience that meant a great deal to our son As we transitioned to middle school where we understood we were understandably anxious However, Glasgow middle school made the transition seamless through strong coordination between schools thoughtful outreach and Support for AAP non-AAP and IEP students our son entered sixth grade confident and thriving Principal Barron or her team have been exceptional the community matters Students from our neighborhood enter middle school already knowing classmates teachers and even staff because these schools function as a true pyramid They do not walk those hallways as strangers We are deeply invested in the schools in our community

I have served many years as PTA boards at both schools and I have invited I've been invited to participate in justice-related scholarship funds effort created by long-standing community members and neighbors We are a small community about a hundred homes where families grow up together often across generations within the same pyramid I respectfully ask the board to preserve our current school assignments and allow our children to continue their planned educational journey together.

Before rezoning our neighborhood is revisited, I invite you to visit our community, meet our students and families, and hear our stories firsthand. Leah Sumner. Good evening. My name is Leah Sumner. Thank you for your time and consideration today.

I reside in SBA 2810 within the Tyson's Green neighborhood and an FCPS parent. In the first three proposals, we were appropriately aligned with neighbors to Madison High School. But after addressing other communities' needs while excluding us, in the end, the current boundary proposal is a worst-case scenario than our current boundaries and further isolates and silos us away from the Vienna neighborhoods that we are geographically and community-aligned to via natural boundaries, location, community organizations, and walkability.

Understanding that West Friar is still a split feeder, it is more beneficial to the children and the community that students are aligned where natural and community boundaries are for children's well-being, safety, and in alignment with boundary objectives. I appreciate you allowing our children to have priority transfer, which acknowledges our alignment to the other neighborhoods, but this still keeps us siloed and fragments our Tyson's Green community.

Additionally, I appreciate we will be under future consideration, but I implore you to consider our inclusion with other community members now, especially considering the current Tyson's development that will certainly impact Marshall High School's capacity in the immediate future and who we are separated from by major roads and natural boundaries. As such, we should be aligned to Madison versus Marshall. Further, I want to address it is not too late to do the right and logical thing for our current children versus one impacted five years down the road. I request that our representatives not

forget to represent Tyson's Green and advocate for us in alignment with FCPS objectives and align SPA 2810 with our neighbors to Madison High School. Thank you. Natalie Cronin, Natalie Cronin, Natalie Cronin. Lauren Garris, Lauren
Garris, Lauren Garris, Margot Wong. Ms. Wong can you hear us? You are muted right
now. Ms. Wong, can you hear us? Good evening. My name is Margo Wong, and I am the IB coordinator at Belvedere Elementary School, as well as the parent of a first grade student at Belvedere.

Belvedere is proud to offer IB's primary years program, and we are one of just two elementary schools in FCPS to offer this program. Currently, our school is part of the Justice Pyramid, and when students leave Belvedere, they continue their IB education at both Glasgow Middle School and Justice High School. Very recently a scenario was proposed that would cause some students from Belvedere Elementary School to leave our pyramid and for some also end their time with IB. I thank Dr. Reed and the school board for their careful considerations of all scenarios and the impacts

any changes have on our community. For our tiny section of FCPS, turning Belvedere Elementary school into a split feeder has long-lasting impacts. With just two schools offering students the opportunity to begin IB in preschool or kindergarten and continue through 12th grade, I urge the board to keep Belvedere Elementary School in the Justice Pyramid in any future boundary adjustments so that all Belvedere students have that opportunity. Thank you. Ellen Serafini.

Good evening. My name is Ellen Serafini, and first I want to thank FCPS and members of our school board for hosting this meeting of community members in light of recently proposed and now postponed boundary changes.

I truly value the opportunity to share my perspective as an educational stakeholder, both as a parent of two kids at Belvedere Elementary School and an active PTA member, as well as a local university educator educator who trains pre service and in service public school teachers. In the six largest and one of the most linguistically and culturally diverse public school systems in the U.S., the need to collectively advocate for educational equity and the academic achievement of all our students and kids is nothing if not a complex endeavor.

As a kid who grew up in the south without access to AAP or IB and only one high school, I recognize I am privileged to have access to these forms of education for my own children and to have the agency to advocate for their needs I also believe that the best forms of education are practiced transparently through dialogue and sustained home and community engagement and as members of our vastly dynamic and diverse community of practice I am hopeful that going forward in the boundary proposal process all stakeholders voices continue to be heard and members of the school board strive to maintain transparency and timely

communication in seeking ways to address overcrowding and capacity issues without sacrificing the curricular integrity of our IB pyramid or the socio-emotional well-being of our children. Margaret Summers, Margaret

Summers, Margaret Summers, Heather McCain. Good evening, Chair Anderson, Superintendent Reed and members of the board. My name is Heather McCain and I am here as a representative of the Walney Oaks HOA board in our community. I've stood before you previously with frustration but tonight I'm here with a very different message. Thank you. On behalf of the families in Walney Oaks I

want to formally withdraw our opposition to the proposed boundary changes. We want to express our sincere gratitude to the Boundary Review Advisory Committee and this board for listening to our concerns and incorporating Walney Oaks into the final plan. For decades our neighborhood felt like an afterthought a literal attendance island on the map. By correcting this anomaly and addressing the split feeder patterns at Brookfield Elementary and Franklin Middle, you have done more than just move lines on a map.

You have restored logic and safety to our students' commutes. You have prioritized student cohorting and social stability. And most importantly, you have shown that the public engagement process actually works. It is rare in local government to feel so clearly heard.

We recognize the immense pressure and the difficult math involved in these decisions. By choosing to include Walney Oaks, you have ensured that our children will transition through the Chantilly pyramid alongside their neighbors and peers exactly as this process intended. We know that is not easy and it is not possible to make everyone happy but we are grateful for this step forward.
We are excited to move forward as a more cohesive part of our school community. Thank you for your leadership your late nights and your commitment to this process.

Good evening. I'm here on behalf of my two kids who happen to be among the nearly 1,700 who would be realigned based on the recommendations. And why I'm here is because I want you to hear how much I fully support these recommendations. I really implore the school board to go ahead and approve this tonight if, well, actually not if possible.

Please just approve it. I would say that the impact, I think some people have focused on the impact on the 1,700 realigned kids. But I really feel like it is lost that this impacts all 183,000 kids within Fairfax County Public Schools. And those impacts are positive. This whole effort has been all about balancing capacity.

Keeping communities together ensuring equitable access to programs. I will say as we have gotten closer to tonight's vote. The uncertainty felt by so many students and parents and teachers has really increased anxiety and a feeling of lack of control. I have a middle schooler who does not know for sure which high school she's going to next year.

She doesn't know which open house to go to. She doesn't know what courses she's going to be able to select from. You have parents who need to have time to make informed decisions about whether or not their kids are going to stay at their current school or their realigned school. Making a decision tonight, you have the opportunity to really alleviate so much concern for so many people within this community.

I will say, as we heard earlier, this has been an 18-month process. There have been 48 in-person, virtual, and hybrid meetings. There have been three public hearings. There have been 27,000 comments on the various tools online. And honestly, I cannot imagine the number of emails and calls and conversations you all have had, the superintendent has had, or the 96 BRAC volunteers have had.

I have to say I was incredibly uplifted to see the changes after the first public hearing. It really showed that the superintendent and her team are here to listen. They take that feedback to heart. They listen, they assess, they take action. I will say as a compliance nerd, I was very excited to see pen to paper committing to addressing certain targeted areas in the future.
And I just ask you please these are informed substantiated and optimized recommendations please vote yes. Chris Mitchell. Chris Mitchell. Chris Mitchell.
Carrie pork high. Good evening my name is Carrie pork high and I'm a parent from Cardinal Forest Elementary.

What we appreciate that the West Springfield boundary decision is on hold. It is deeply concerning that a proposal was ever considered to increase a school already over capacity to 108 percent. While nearby schools remain well below capacity with some even slated to enrollment reductions placing the burden of overcrowding on a single school to preserve preferred school assignments for certain communities directly contradicts FCPS goals of equity and smacks of discrimination.

Even more troubling all four proposed scenarios remove most single family homes from the Cardinal Forest boundary leaving behind an island of townhomes condos and apartments. This fundamentally alters the fabric of both our school and our community and raises serious concerns about diversity, particularly when those homes are being shifted to schools planned for decreased capacity.

Families are left asking who set these priorities and how such an obvious and significant impact on one community when unnoticed by the board. These decisions have real consequences. Overcrowded classrooms, continued reliance on trailers, experienced educators leaving, and strain on basic functions like lunch and recess are not hypothetical.

They are our current reality. Further increasing enrollment at our school will push it past the breaking point while other schools are positioned to thrive. My question for the board is this, what will you do this year to achieve a more equitable outcome? What criteria and data will ensure capacity pressures are not disproportionately placed on one community?

How will the board ensure the boundary review process is transparent and aligned with FCPS priorities of community cohesion and equitable access to quality instruction? Most importantly, how will meaningful representation from our affected communities be included in the final recommendations.

We appreciate the pause, but now we need a clear plan that restores trust. There is no scenario in which increasing Cardinal Forest to 108% capacity is acceptable for our community. Thank you for your time.
